title: Paul Ash's stage manager MacDermott and the piano position
summary: The stage manager wants the piano moved to the other side; Bubbles tells him the act does not fit, and they negotiate.

story.theme_name: Pianists: who played, who influenced whom
story.community_name: Who played piano: the pianists musicians remembered

blocks.x: left side, you know. So when Buck was going to rehearse the music that's what they told him about the piano then. He comes upstairs -- I'm unpacking -- he comes upstairs to tell me about it and I says, "Don't cry about it, we're not on the stage, we're not doing nothin' yet. Don't cry about it, I'll go down with ya and we'll see what it is." So he takes me downstairs, "Show me the fella," his name is MacDermott. Okay, I'll take care of it. Soon as I got a chance and there was a lull in what he was doing, I went on the stage and I said, "Mr. MacDermott, my partner was telling me that you want to move the piano from where it is on the left side to the right side. "Yes, I saw your act so-and-so-and-so-and-so. I said, "Yeah, really?" Mh-hm, mh-hm -- and the band is listening all the people on the stage in the show is listening, they're sitting in the audience and the band is in the bandstand. I says, "Yeah, really?" Well, when he finished talking, I says, "Well, I'm sorry, Mr. MacDermott, Buck and Bubbles don't fit your
show and you just count us out until we can fit, okay? And I walked off the stage. Now, I'm finished.

When I get off stage, the stage manager over there says that the reason why he wants to change the piano is because the piano is in the way for them to move this lever for the band to go down forward, move the band down forward and put it back. I said, yeah, when they do that, when they put the band back -- bandstand back, where does Buck and Bubbles go? The band is a success and they put them back. Now we come on in a whole new setting that we know nothing about, and where do we stand? What'll they do for us? Nothing. Don't fit. With the piano over there, we can't go on, that's it. That's the end, we have to leave. So we go on upstairs deciding on we don't fit the show.
Finally the stage manager says they did get their heads together we'll put the piano on the side of the stage where they want it.
